findings.guest_result: The new guest-side probe enumerated VioSerialPort instance IDs through PnPUtil and Control\\DeviceClasses, then proved `\\.\Global\org.qemu.guest_agent.0` is openable with CreateFile. It also showed the exact registry-derived `...&02...` interface path is openable, while the sibling `...&01...` path returns access denied and the naive `\\.\Global\vport0p2` / `\\.\vport0p2` aliases remain missing.

findings.command: sc start QEMU-GA; sc query QEMU-GA; virsh qemu-agent-command ...; virsh qemu-monitor-command ... --hmp 'info chardev'
findings.guest_result: QEMU-GA reached `RUNNING` in the guest after the open-path probe.
findings.host_result: Host-side `guest-ping` still failed with `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error`, and HMP still showed the qga chardev as `disconnected`.

findings.guest_result: The launcher selected the openable `...&02...` DeviceClasses path from the probe output and started `qemu-ga.exe -v -m virtio-serial -p <exact path>` into the same continuous `debug: dispatch` foreground loop seen in earlier alias-based repros.
findings.host_result: Even under the exact openable `...&02...` path, `guest-ping` still returned `QEMU guest agent is not available due to an error` and HMP still reported `disconnected`.

conclusion: The remaining KVM guest-control blocker is no longer Windows virtio-serial path resolution. The default qga alias and the exact `...&02...` DeviceClasses-derived interface path are both openable inside the guest, yet host-side qga control still stays in the same disconnected/error state. The unresolved layer is now post-open qga runtime/protocol or libvirt/KVM handshake behavior rather than path discovery.
